```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 10_confidence_intervals_ci
title: >
  Calculate the CI
questions:
  - id: single_sample_ci
    type: free-response
    prompt: >
      Now calculate a 99% confidence interval for students' mean hours of sleep.
      The sample mean is still 7.31 hours and the standard error is still 0.265
      hours, but for 99% confidence, z = 2.58. How does the interval compare to
      the 95% interval?
    answer: >
      The margin of error is 2.58 * 0.265 = 0.68, so the interval is
      7.31 +/- 0.68, or about [6.63, 7.99]. It is wider than the 95%
      interval of about [6.79, 7.83].
    explanation: >
      Only z changes: the sample mean and standard error stay the same. A higher
      confidence level uses a larger z, which gives a larger margin of error and
      a wider interval.
```
